data.description: Core thesis of the bench: representation sensitivity. The calculus is trivial; the question is whether models reason over structure or over token statistics of the surface form. Add a handful of new text dialects as FormRenderer subclasses registered in renderers/__init__.py. Candidate directions (pick during planning, ~3-5): indentation/tree notation, XML/HTML-style open-close tags, JSON nesting, natural-language containment prose ('a circle containing two circles...'), emoji/unicode bracket vocabularies (notebooks/emoji-examples.txt has prior art), word-delimited brackets (BEGIN/END), whitespace-noise variants. Each renderer must be structure-preserving (isomorphic to the canonical form), deterministic under a seed, and covered by tests mirroring tests/test_renderers.py patterns. Decision context: paired design — same underlying forms across all dialects — is already the sampling strategy, so renderers must not alter form identity.

The benchmark tests whether models reason about structure or about surface tokens. The calculus stays simple; the representation varies. Add 3 to 5 new text dialects as FormRenderer subclasses, registered in renderers/__init__.py.

Candidate dialects (choose during planning):
- indentation or tree notation
- XML-style open and close tags
- JSON nesting
- plain-English descriptions of containment, such as 'a circle containing two circles'
- emoji or unicode bracket alphabets (notebooks/emoji-examples.txt has earlier examples)
- word brackets such as BEGIN and END

Each renderer must keep the structure identical to the canonical form, be deterministic under a seed, and have tests like those in tests/test_renderers.py. We run the same forms through every dialect and compare results pair by pair, so a renderer must never change which form a sample represents. Read the DB-4 description before designing: new renderers should fit the planned composable pipeline.

Read .lattice/notes/design-decisions-2026-07-04.md first. It binds this task.

Add new text dialects as FormRenderer subclasses registered in renderers/__init__.py. The parens family already has canonical, multi-bracket and mismatched-bracket variants. Sexpr starts its own 'pattern' family.

Scope:
- text archetypes for families from the taxonomy that have natural text forms: indentation or tree notation, word brackets, plain-English containment prose
- a handful of novel dialects built on self-similar structures from mathematics or nature (for example L-systems or nested clause embedding); propose candidates in the plan and justify them
- every dialect encodes containment only; distractor features (like bracket mismatch) are welcome but the containment structure must stay isomorphic to the source form

Each renderer must be deterministic under a seed, round-trip or otherwise machine-verify structure preservation, and have tests like tests/test_renderers.py. Design renderers as archetype generators that the DB-4 variation pipeline can wrap; read the DB-4 description before designing.

data.body: Holding planning until the rendering architecture doc from the DB-4 ultracode run lands. Archetype designs must target that pipeline.

Flagging a conflict found during planning: rendering-architecture-2026-07-04.md's section 'How DB-2 and DB-3 build archetypes on this' assigns spatial families (paths, blocks, trees, graph, map, rooms) to DB-2 and novel self-similar dialects to DB-3. The live task descriptions (checked via lattice show on both) say the opposite: DB-2 is text dialect families plus novel picks, DB-3 is the visual/spatial families. The titles were renamed after the architecture note was written, so the live descriptions are treated as authoritative in the DB-2 plan. Worth a look before DB-3 planning starts so nobody re-derives the same confusion.

Adversarial plan review (reviewer-b). VERDICT: PASS WITH FIXES.

Interface guessing (axis 1): OK. Every DB-4 symbol DB-2 names (FormNode, containment_relation, relation_hash, Primitive, BaseRender, Archetype/Injector protocols, ComposedRenderer, ARCHETYPE_REGISTRY/INJECTOR_REGISTRY, DialectSpec, verify, emit, register_renderer) appears in the DB-4 plan; names match. Phase A/B split (Phase A depends only on lofbench.core, which really exposes string_to_form + generate_form_string + DIFFICULTY_CONFIGS; width-9/depth-9 claim verified against lunatic/extra tiers) is the right hedge and produces mergeable code today. Good catch on predicate() being declared unconditionally yet unused for text — genuine open Q for DB-4.

Swap confusion (axis 2): resolved correctly. DB-2 follows the live task split (text + novel) not the arch doc's reversed labels, consistent with DB-3. BUT: rna_arc ownership is contradicted between the two plans. DB-2 calls rna_arc 'DB-3s worked example 4'; DB-3 explicitly disclaims it as DB-2s (novel nature dialect). Neither plan schedules building rna_arc@1 — it is ORPHANED. Since the decisions doc asks for 'a handful of novel dialects from maths/nature' and DB-2s three novels are all text, the one spatial novel falls through the crack. FIX: DB-2 either owns rna_arc@1 explicitly or the orchestrator assigns it; drop the mis-attribution to DB-3.

Determinism (axis 3): under-pinned for prose + clause_embedding, as the plan half-admits. (a) The center-embedding psycholinguistic justification is oversold: the actual grammar right-branches relative clauses joined by 'and' ('the fox that watches the rabbit that hides and the mouse that hides'), which does NOT reproduce center-embedding processing difficulty ('the rat the cat chased squeaked'). Either change the grammar to genuine center-embedding or drop the human-limit adversarial claim. (b) Neither grammar is fully pinned: prose sibling-joining when children differ (comma? 'and'? order), the 'two empty boxes' collapse boundary, numeral words 0-9, and tree_indent's comment-line syntax are all unspecified — exactly where an unseeded silent choice breaks determinism. Pin the grammars formally before Phase A implementation.

Structure preservation (axis 4): text round-trip parse_X(render_X(s))==string_to_form(s) is genuinely discriminative for all five. Residual complicit-parser risk (dialect's own reader could share a bug with its writer) is low because containment_relation is sibling-order-insensitive, so the only bugs that matter are depth errors, which an honest reader catches. Acceptable.

Sequencing: 'Phase B blocked on DB-4 step 1' is imprecise. Phase B needs DialectSpec + named-factory registration, which land in DB-4 M2, not M1. DB-4's own plan says M1+M2 is the unblock. Restate as M1+M2.

Taxonomy (axis 5): DB-2 covers parens (word-brackets variant on parens@1) + trees (text tree_indent, coexists with DB-3s spatial trees, no collision) + three novels (biopolymer text, prose, embedding). No family orphaned here except the rna_arc spatial-novel gap above.

PASS WITH FIXES: (1) resolve rna_arc orphan/ownership; (2) reconcile center-embedding justification with the right-branching grammar; (3) fully pin prose + clause + tree_indent grammars (joining, numerals, comment syntax) before implementation; (4) restate Phase B blocker as DB-4 M1+M2. None plan-level; all implementation-level.

Review fixes applied: pinned rna_arc@1 to DB-3 (DB-2's novel scope is text-only, accepted). Flagged the clause_embedding grammar as right-branching, not genuine centre-embedding; prefers fixing to genuine centre-embedding, implementer must pin it. Added a grammar-pinning requirement (sibling-joining, empty-boxes collapse boundary, numerals, comment syntax) before Phase A. Restated the Phase B blocker as DB-4 M1+M2, not 'step 1'.

Phase A complete on feat/DB-2-text-dialects-phase-a (commit aa4ad3b), implemented in a stale worktree (base commit 657eb61, pre-lattice-migration but src/lofbench identical to current lattice branch HEAD — verified via diff before starting).

Five render_X/parse_X pairs, standalone, lofbench.core only, no Archetype/registry wiring:
- src/lofbench/dialects_text/rna_dotbracket.py
- src/lofbench/dialects_text/tree_indent.py
- src/lofbench/dialects_text/word_brackets.py
- src/lofbench/dialects_text/prose.py
- src/lofbench/dialects_text/clause_embedding.py
- tests/test_text_dialects_standalone.py

Grammar pinned in each module docstring before coding, per the binding requirement:
- prose/clause_embedding: explicit sibling lists are count-prefixed ("N things: ..." / "N creatures namely ...") rather than open-ended and-joined. A bare recursive-descent reader cannot invert nested and-joined lists unambiguously once a list member is itself a multi-child mark with its own list — reading the count first turns "consume while I see a separator" into "consume exactly N", which is unambiguous at any depth. Collapse-to-plural ("two empty boxes") is pinned to apply only when every sibling is a bare leaf.
- clause_embedding: implements genuine centre-embedding per the review fix (child's full clause, including its own trailing verb, nests inside the subject position before this level's verb — verbs stack at the sentence end, deepest first, e.g. "...sleeps watches watches."), replacing the plan's right-branching example. Width (>1 children) generalises via the same count-prefix technique as prose, since plain conjunction is ambiguous the same way.
- tree_indent: comment lines (leading '#') skipped unconditionally regardless of indent, pinned for the Phase B jitter injector.
- rna_dotbracket: two-line sequence/structure format pinned; parser strips '.' filler unconditionally though Phase A's base render never emits it.

Deviation from plan's literal prose/clause_embedding examples: both now use count-prefixed lists for width>1 (plan's flat examples only showed the identical-leaf collapse case, which is unaffected and matches verbatim). This was necessary to make the "explicit list" branch the plan calls for actually invertible — flagging since it's a implementer judgment call the plan explicitly delegated.

Gates green: uv run pytest -x -q → 5126 passed (5070 in the new suite: edge cases + 200 generated forms/tier x5 tiers x5 dialects, plus determinism and disambiguation regressions). uv run ruff check on new files clean (repo-wide ruff check has 15 pre-existing errors in analysis.py/core.py/sexpr.py/svg_circle_renderer.py/datasets/factory.py/test_scorers.py, confirmed present before this change via git stash -u diff — out of scope, not touched, boundary forbids editing renderers/).

Phase B (Archetype wrapping, registry, DialectSpec, injectors, provenance) remains blocked on DB-4 landing M1 (core abstractions) and M2 (registry widening + DialectSpec). Do not mark DB-2 done on Phase A alone per the plan's own acceptance criteria (registry-reachable, provenance recorded).

REVIEW (phase A, cold review by agent:claire-reviewer-db2) — VERDICT: PASS, no rework.

Gates: uv run pytest -x -q => 5126 passed (matches claim). ruff (via uvx) on the 5 new modules + test file => All checks passed. Diff is scoped: only src/lofbench/dialects_text/{__init__,rna_dotbracket,tree_indent,word_brackets,prose,clause_embedding}.py + tests/test_text_dialects_standalone.py. No model calls, no touches outside scope.

Grammar pins: all five modules carry an explicit binding 'Grammar pin' docstring section (rna, tree_indent, word_brackets, prose, clause_embedding). Requirement met.

Zero unseeded branch points: verified every conditional in every render path is a pure function of the form. Only seeded draw is rna's sequence line (rng.choice over ACGU); structure line is form_string char-for-char. prose/clause/tree/word use no rng at all. The rng-is-None fallback is a guarded, documented default (caller always passes rng in tests). Clean.

Centre-embedding: genuine for the single-child chain. ((())) => 'the creature that the creature that the creature sleeps watches watches.' — child clauses (incl. their own verbs) nest inside the subject NP before the parent verb, so verbs stack leaf-first at the end (sleeps/watches/watches). Hand-derived ((())()) from the docstring grammar and it matches code byte-for-byte: 'the creature that two creatures namely the creature that the creature sleeps watches and the creature sleeps watches.' Width is handled by the pinned count-prefixed conjoined-subject deviation, documented in the docstring.

Round-trips are genuine inverses: parse_* are real recursive-descent / indent-stack / bracket readers, no memoization or caching of render inputs. Property tests cover deep nesting (depth-9 boundary) and wide fan-out (width-9 boundary) plus 200 generated forms/tier.

COLLISION CHECK (adversarial, /tmp scratch): exhaustively enumerated all 2695 distinct canonical forms up to 7 marks PLUS 500 generated forms per DIFFICULTY tier. For all five dialects: roundtrip_fail=0 and distinct_renders == distinct_forms (2695/2695). No two distinct forms render identically. Paired-design safe on this sample. rna checked on structure line only (sequence is decorative random).

COUNT-LEAK (stimulus-validity, NON-BLOCKING — flag for measurement doc): prose and clause_embedding both emit the child count as an explicit numeral word at every multi-child node ('two creatures namely...', 'N things:', and the all-leaf collapse 'two empty boxes'). This means the width dimension is stated, not inferred — a strong structural hint that trivializes width for these two dialects. The stated justification (bare and-joined nested lists are ambiguous to an LL parser) is TRUE — a delimiter is genuinely required. But the count-prefix is not the ONLY disambiguator; explicit closing/bracketing tokens would resolve the ambiguity without leaking cardinality. So the leak is a consequence of this specific design choice, not strictly forced. rna/tree_indent/word_brackets do NOT leak count. Recommend the measurement doc note that width-sensitivity results for prose.* and embedding.* dialects are confounded by the explicit count.

Phase A does NOT complete DB-2 (acceptance criteria require Phase B registry/provenance wiring, blocked on DB-4 M1+M2). Leaving status at review. Orchestrator recommendation: route DB-2 back to in_progress, gated on DB-4 landing M1+M2, per the plan's sequencing section.

Phase A reviewed (pass) and merged at e06582e. Routing to in_progress for phase B: archetype wrapping and named DialectSpec registration against the merged pipeline (M1+M2 on lattice). Reviewer flag carried forward: count-prefix in prose and clause_embedding leaks child cardinality; width sensitivity for those two dialects is confounded — recorded for the measurement doc.

Phase B complete on feat/DB-2-text-dialects-phase-b (commit 3aa8285), branched off lattice tip d60714e (M1/M2 pipeline + phase A both present).

All five dialects wrapped as Archetypes + registered as named DialectSpecs, reachable via get_renderer:
- biopolymer.rna-dotbracket-v1 / -filler-v1 (archetype rna_dotbracket@1, injector unpaired_filler)
- trees.indent-v1 / -jitter-v1 (archetype tree_indent@1, injector indent_style_jitter)
- parens.word-brackets-v1 / -mismatched-v1 (archetype word_brackets@1 -- see deviation below, injector word_delimiter_swap)
- prose.containment-v1 / -jitter-v1 (archetype prose@1, injector synonym_jitter)
- embedding.center-clause-v1 / -jitter-v1 (archetype clause_embedding@1, injector vocabulary_jitter)

Files touched: src/lofbench/dialects_text/{__init__,_common(new),rna_dotbracket,tree_indent,word_brackets,prose,clause_embedding}.py, one append-only hook (import + register_text_dialects() call) at the tail of src/lofbench/renderers/__init__.py, new tests/test_text_dialects_pipeline.py. No edits to pipeline core (archetype.py/composed.py/verify.py/etc.), lofsite/, or legacy renderers.

Two deliberate deviations, both documented inline in code + plan-relevant:
1. word_brackets: parens@1 doesn't exist yet (DB-4 M3-M5 scope, out of my boundary) -- registered a provisional word_brackets@1 archetype instead so the dialect actually works today. One-line follow-up to repoint once parens@1 lands.
2. M1's verify() hardcodes the canonical-parens text_reader (per-archetype readers are M4/M5 scope per architecture doc). rna_dotbracket's structure line happens to be literal parens so its structure_verified is genuinely accurate through the real pipeline; the other four dialects' structure_verified is False through ComposedRenderer today (not a bug -- confirmed and pinned in a test) because the pipeline has no way yet to plug in their own parser. Used each dialect's own parse_X as the real verification path per the brief ("round-trip verification wired as the text verification path"), cross-checked against the pipeline's actual archetype.build() output.

Design choice: every injector rebuilds fresh from the FormNode tree (ignoring the incoming base) rather than doing string surgery on the base render -- keeps jittered variants safe by construction (e.g. tree_indent's off-side rule) instead of needing to reason about post-hoc offset patching. Caught and fixed one real bug this way during testing: an earlier draft drew the indent increment per-child instead of per-parent, which let sibling lines land at different columns and broke the off-side rule.

Gates: uv run pytest -x -q -> 6152 passed (existing tests unmodified and green, including tests/test_text_dialects_standalone.py's phase A suite). ruff check clean on all touched files (15 pre-existing errors remain elsewhere in the repo, unrelated to this task, not touched). No-jitter archetype builds verified byte-identical to their Phase A render_X counterparts across edge cases + generated forms at all DIFFICULTY_CONFIGS tiers.

REVIEW phase B (cold review, agent:claire-reviewer-db2b) — VERDICT: PASS on its own branch; a text_reader merge-fix is REQUIRED before/at the DB-4 M3-M5 merge (details below). Reviewed commit 3aa8285 on feat/DB-2-text-dialects-phase-b (base d60714e).

GATES: uv run pytest --ignore=tests/test_lofsite.py -> 6152 passed (matches claim). test_lofsite.py collection error is PRE-EXISTING (last touched at base d60714e; missing 'starlette', a DB-6 dep) — not DB-2B's fault. ruff clean on all touched files.

ADVERSARIAL (all green): (1) all ten named dialects resolve via get_renderer and round-trip (()()); (2) determinism across FRESH renderer+rng objects for every canonical AND jitter variant (rendered + metadata identical); (3) 100 generated forms/dialect (incl. filler/jitter injector output) parse back to the exact source form — 0 failures; (4) negative path is GENUINE not just asserted: test_broken_archetype_fails_pipeline_verify drives a broken archetype through the real ComposedRenderer -> structure_verified False + hashes differ (I re-confirmed independently), and the four parser-corruption cases genuinely reject; (5) structure_verified pins correct through the real pipeline — rna_dotbracket True (structure line is literal parens the canonical M1 reader picks up), the other four False (M1 verify hardcodes the canonical reader, documented honestly in the test module docstring, with each dialect's own parse_X standing in as the verification path); (6) provenance carries dialect_id/family/modality/format + both relation hashes for all ten.

MERGE RISK vs feat/DB-4-pipeline-m3-m5 (fec3423) — the important part. Only ONE file overlaps textually: src/lofbench/renderers/__init__.py (both append at EOF; trivial 'keep both hunks' conflict — recommend DB-4's 'from . import archetypes, injectors' first, then DB-2B's register_text_dialects()). dialects_text/* is DB-2B-only; pipeline/archetypes/injectors are DB-4-only — no other textual conflicts. BUT a hard SEMANTIC break: (a) M3-M5's composed.render() does text_reader=getattr(archetype,'text_reader',None) then RAISES RuntimeError if structure_verified is False before injectors. DB-2B's four non-parens archetypes (tree_indent/word_brackets/prose/clause_embedding) define NO text_reader (grep confirms none), so post-merge the canonical reader sees zero marks in their payloads -> verify False -> render RAISES for every non-void form. That is 8 of the 10 specs unrenderable (both rna specs survive). It is NOT a mere verify-flag flip as the pinned test's comment anticipated — it is a crash. FIX (merge-time, cannot be applied on DB-2B's base since it needs DB-4's nodes_from_parsed): add text_reader = staticmethod(lambda s: nodes_from_parsed(parse_X(s))) to each of the four archetypes (word_brackets should wrap parse_word_brackets_mismatched to cover both matched+mismatched), following the exact pattern DB-4's archetypes/parens.py::bracket_agnostic_reader establishes; then flip the pinned structure_verified/pipeline-reliable flags for those four from False to True. (b) word_brackets@1 vs parens@1: no collision — disjoint archetype keys (word_brackets@1 vs parens@1), disjoint dialect_ids (parens.word-brackets-* vs parens.canonical/jitter/noisy-*), disjoint injector names. The provisional word_brackets@1 is SOUND (parens@1 didn't exist on DB-2B's base; registering against a missing key would KeyError and fail acceptance). HOWEVER the implementer's breadcrumb that it can later be 'retired by a one-line repoint to parens@1' is WRONG: parens@1 renders literal parens and bracket_swap only swaps single-glyph BRACKET_PAIRS; neither can emit BEGIN/END word tokens with separators. word_brackets@1 must STAY; the follow-up note should be corrected. (c) covered above — single trivial __init__.py conflict.

DEVIATIONS: both sound engineering under parallel dev, not corners. Provisional word_brackets@1: correct call for independent mergeability (only the retirement claim is mistaken). verify-False-pinned-as-test: honest and well-documented, does not paper over the gap — but it under-estimated the merge consequence (raise, not flip). Note the brief's 'round-trip verification wired as the text verification path' is met at the TEST level for the four dialects, not the PIPELINE level (text_reader unset) — unavoidable given DB-2B's base verify() has no text_reader kwarg; that wiring IS the merge fix.

RECOMMENDATION: PASS, no implementation rework on the branch as-is. Do NOT mark done — leaving at review pending the DB-4 merge. Merge order: land DB-4 M3-M5 FIRST, then land DB-2B on top applying (i) the four text_readers, (ii) the pinned-flag flips to True, (iii) the trivial __init__.py both-hunks resolution, (iv) corrected word_brackets breadcrumb. All four are mechanical and belong to the merge commit, not to reopening this task's implementation.

Merge attempted (feat/DB-2-text-dialects-phase-b --no-ff into lattice, on top of 9b47800) and then ABORTED per the reviewer's stop condition -- lattice is unchanged at 9b47800, still green (6213 passed).

What was done before the abort: resolved the one expected conflict in src/lofbench/renderers/__init__.py (kept both appended hunks: existing imports, then DB-2B's register_text_dialects() call last). Then applied all four reviewer-mandated fixes: (i) added Archetype.text_reader = staticmethod(lambda s: nodes_from_parsed(parse_X(s))) to tree_indent/word_brackets/prose/clause_embedding (word_brackets wraps parse_word_brackets_mismatched so both matched and mismatched modes verify); (ii) flipped the eight pinned structure_verified=False entries in tests/test_text_dialects_pipeline.py's DIALECTS dict to True and rewrote the module/test docstrings explaining why; (iv) corrected the word_brackets.py breadcrumb -- word_brackets@1 is permanent, parens@1 is not a drop-in replacement (single-glyph brackets vs BEGIN/END word tokens). Verified all ten dialects render clean (structure_verified True, zero raises) over 20 generated forms each before running the full suite.

Why it was aborted: tests/test_text_dialects_pipeline.py::TestParseBackCatchesCorruption::test_broken_archetype_fails_pipeline_verify fails with RuntimeError instead of the assertion it expects. Root cause is orthogonal to the four fixes above -- this DB-2B test asserts a broken archetype's render() *returns* RenderedForm with metadata['structure_verified'] is False, but DB-4 M3-M5's ComposedRenderer.render() (already merged, see composed.py:99) raises RuntimeError immediately when the pre-injector build fails verification, and never returns in that case (its own docstring: 'structure_verified in the stamped provenance is always true for a returned render'). The broken-archetype fixture has no text_reader attribute and isn't touched by any of the four mandated fixes, so this is a genuine DB-4/DB-2B semantic mismatch the merge protocol didn't cover, not a regression from this merge's own changes.

All step-3 work (conflict resolution + all four fixes, internally consistent and passing everywhere else) is preserved uncommitted in Saved working directory and index state WIP on lattice: 9b47800 Merge DB-3: eight visual family archetypes with exact-arithmetic predicates [reviewed, pass] on this exact checkout (/var/home/kwalerie/dev/fractal/distinction-bench, branch lattice) as stash@{0} 'WIP on lattice: 9b47800 Merge DB-3...'. To resume: git stash show --stat stash@{0} to inspect, redo the --no-ff merge (single conflict, same resolution as here), pull the fixed files from stash (git show :3:<path> per file, since a plain checkout/pop will re-conflict against the fresh merge), then resolve test_broken_archetype_fails_pipeline_verify -- most likely by rewriting it to assert pytest.raises(RuntimeError) rather than inspecting a returned result, since that matches M4's documented contract. DB-2 status left at 'review', not moved to done.

Merge landed at aa99439 (Merge: 55498e3 + 3aa8285). All four DB-4/DB-2B merge-time fixes from claire-reviewer-db2b's review confirmed present (text_reader on tree_indent/word_brackets/prose/clause_embedding; DIALECTS dict's 8 pinned structure_verified flags flipped True; renderers/__init__.py both-hunks conflict resolution; word_brackets.py breadcrumb corrected to state parens@1 is not a drop-in and word_brackets@1 is permanent). Fifth fix applied at merge time (orchestrator call): TestParseBackCatchesCorruption::test_broken_archetype_fails_pipeline_verify rewritten -- DB-4 M3-M5's ComposedRenderer.render raises RuntimeError immediately on pre-injector verify failure and never returns a result (composed.py's own docstring: structure_verified is always true for a returned render), so the old assert-on-returned-metadata shape was incompatible with the already-merged M4 contract. Test now checks the relation-hash mismatch via a direct low-level verify() call (same call composed.py makes internally), then asserts pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='failed containment verification') on renderer.render(). Docstring updated to state the M4 contract explicitly. Also fixed one merge-introduced (not pre-existing) ruff I001 finding in renderers/__init__.py via isort:off/on markers around the append-only DB-3/DB-4/DB-2B import block, preserving exact ordering and per-import comments (same pattern as 55498e3's archetypes/__init__.py fix). Verification: ten-dialect render loop (20 generated forms/dialect, 200 total) zero raises, structure_verified True throughout; uv run pytest -x -q -> 7184 passed; uvx ruff check src tests -> 14 errors, matching pre-existing baseline exactly, no new findings. stash@{0} (claire-merge-waveb's WIP) dropped after gates passed. .lattice/ pre-existing uncommitted working-tree state left untouched throughout.
